answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity in sunk compute: admission requires each new wallet to solve a randomized proof-of-work puzzle tuned so one attempt costs more than the expected payout of a fresh account. Attackers churning thousands of identities burn real GPU-hours at the oasis edge of profitability while honest agents, answering once like a black onyx stone set firm, never notice the cost; the attack cost curve hits its nadir only when fake identities outnumber real ones, which is exactly where slashable stake kicks in.
